title: Delegation poker and the delegation matrix
blurb: Explain how delegation poker agrees decision-making within a team and how the delegation matrix makes decision authority transparent.
question: A team keeps arguing over who may decide on tool choices and when the product owner must be asked. Which technique makes decision authority transparent for each decision area?

teach.body: Self-managing teams still need to know who decides what. Delegation poker is a collaborative technique for defining how decisions are made within teams. The delegation matrix then makes responsibilities and decision-making authority transparent: for each decision area it shows who makes the decision and who is involved. Both are organization practice techniques.

teach.h: From discussion to a visible agreement
How delegation poker is commonly played
teach.body: A widely used version comes from Management 3.0. For each decision, everyone privately picks a card for how much authority should be delegated, then all cards are revealed together, so nobody is swayed by others. People with the highest and lowest choices explain, and the group agrees a level. The idea is the same as estimating together: a shared view, built openly.
teach.cite: PRINCE2 Agile V2 book 7.4.2; background: Management 3.0

teach.caption: Background from Management 3.0, shown as a common example; learn the purpose of the technique for the exam.

teach.body: The delegation matrix makes responsibilities and decision-making authority transparent, which keeps people aligned and reduces confusion. It helps teams see who makes decisions and who is involved, decision area by decision area. That streamlines communication and avoids duplicated effort. Clear roles in turn support teamwork.

teach.h: Where they fit in the project
teach.body: The team delegation matrix is a topic of the project kickoff workshop, where it aims to simplify decision-making and empower self-management. It also sets the boundaries of self-management and shows when decisions must be escalated. Across organizations, a delegation matrix can set clear limits within which people may flex, such as what external advisers may decide or only advise on.

Brightwater Housing Co-operative is building a tenant repairs app with an external design adviser. Decisions keep stalling. In the project kickoff workshop, product owner Jamal Baptiste and the team play delegation poker on six decision areas. They agree the team decides on build tools, the PO decides story order, and the adviser advises on the visual style but does not decide it. The results go into a delegation matrix on the team dashboard.

teach.text: Delegation POKER is the collaborative technique for AGREEING how decisions are made; the delegation MATRIX RECORDS who decides and who is involved per decision area. Neither shows skills (skill matrix) nor estimates effort (planning poker style estimating).

items: Delegation poker: a collaborative technique for defining decision-making within teams (7.4.2).
Delegation matrix: makes responsibilities and decision authority transparent (7.4.3).
Matrix shows who decides and who is involved for each decision area.
Benefits: alignment, less confusion, smoother communication, no duplicated effort.
Kickoff topic 'team delegation matrix': simplify decisions, empower self-management.
Sets boundaries for flexing and escalation, including for external advisers.

summary: You can now explain how delegation poker helps a team agree its decision-making and how the delegation matrix makes that authority transparent. You can also say where they fit and how they differ from the skill matrix.

options: A technique for sizing user stories relative to each other
A collaborative technique for defining decision-making in teams
A game to build team spirit at the end of an iteration
A method for mapping each team member's skills and gaps
A.why: Delegation poker is a collaborative technique for defining decision-making processes within teams (7.4.2).

whyNot.0: Relative sizing of stories is agile estimation, such as story points.
whyNot.2: Team-building games are the 'team building' topic of the team retrospective.
whyNot.3: Mapping skills and gaps is the team skill matrix.

A.q: What does a delegation matrix make transparent?
options: The team's current and planned future skills
Work completed and work remaining in a timebox
Total risk exposure across the iterations
A.why: A delegation matrix makes responsibilities and decision-making authority transparent (7.4.3).

whyNot.1: Current and planned skills are shown in the team skill matrix.
whyNot.2: Work done and remaining is shown on burn charts.
whyNot.3: Total risk exposure over iterations is the cumulative risk burn-down chart.

A.q: Which practice do delegation poker and the delegation matrix belong to?
A.why: Both are techniques of the organization practice (7.4.2, 7.4.3).

whyNot.1: Quality techniques include refactoring, technical debt and testing.
whyNot.2: Plans techniques include story mapping and estimation.

B.q: A team needs to see, for each decision area, who decides and who is involved. Which artifact should it use?
B.why: The delegation matrix helps teams understand who makes decisions and who is involved, by decision area (7.4.3).

whyNot.0: The skill matrix shows capabilities, not who is involved in decisions.
whyNot.1: The project dashboard shows release status, burn charts, risks and issues.
whyNot.3: The release map clusters user stories into releases; it says nothing about decisions.

B.q: What is the stated aim of the 'team delegation matrix' topic in the project kickoff workshop?
options: To map skills and find gaps or overlaps
To simplify decisions and empower self-management
To build familiarity and connections in the team
To give transparency on team progress
B.why: The team delegation matrix topic aims to simplify decision-making and empower self-management (Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: Mapping skills and gaps is the 'team skill matrix' topic.
whyNot.2: Familiarity and connections are the aim of the 'team intro' topic.
whyNot.3: Transparency on team progress is the aim of the 'team dashboards' topic.

B.q:
Which two statements about the delegation matrix are correct?
1. It helps avoid duplication of effort.
2. It records the effort estimate for each user story.
3. It can set limits on what external advisers decide.
4. It replaces the role descriptions management product.
B.why: The matrix streamlines communication and avoids duplicated effort (1), and it can set boundaries such as what external advisers decide or advise on (3) (7.4.3, 4.3.1).

whyNot.0: Statement 2 is wrong: effort estimates come from agile estimation.
whyNot.1: Both are wrong: estimates come from estimation, and role descriptions remain a product.
whyNot.2: Statement 4 is wrong: role descriptions remain a separate organization product.

C.q: A team agrees decision levels by voting privately and revealing together, then wants who decides each area made transparent. Which technique did it use, and which artifact shows that?
C.why: Delegation poker is the collaborative technique for defining decision-making (7.4.2); the delegation matrix makes clear who decides and who is involved per decision area (7.4.3).

whyNot.0: Magic estimation sizes stories; it does not agree decision levels.
whyNot.2: Story mapping breaks products into stories, and the release map plans releases.
whyNot.3: Card-based estimating sizes stories for the team plan, not decision levels.

C.q: An external adviser joins a project and keeps overruling the team on design. What does PRINCE2 Agile suggest to clarify their position?
options: Remove the adviser from the team's planning workshops
Ask the project board to approve each design decision first
Agree a delegation matrix of what they decide or advise on
Add the adviser's design tasks to the team skill matrix
C.why: Set clear boundaries within which people can flex, for example a delegation matrix showing what external advisers decide or advise on (4.3.1, 7.4.3).

whyNot.0: Excluding the adviser loses their input rather than clarifying their authority.
whyNot.1: Escalating every design choice to the board defeats self-management within tolerances.
whyNot.3: The skill matrix shows capabilities, not decision authority.

C.q: Which statement BEST explains why these techniques support self-management in PRINCE2 Agile?
options: They make decision boundaries clear before work starts
They let the team set its own time and cost tolerances
They move all decision authority from the PM to the CPO
They replace the need for escalation to the board
C.why: Knowing the boundaries of self-management and when decisions must be escalated empowers teams (4.5, Table 13.8).

whyNot.1: Time and cost tolerances are set by governance and have zero tolerance by default.
whyNot.2: They clarify decisions within teams; they do not shift authority between PM and CPO.
whyNot.3: Escalation still applies when decisions fall outside agreed boundaries or tolerances.

reteach.title: House rules for flatmates
reteach.question: Four flatmates keep clashing over who can book a cleaner, choose the energy supplier or invite guests. How would you settle it for good?

blocks.body: Everyone secretly picks how much each choice should be left to one person or decided together, then all reveal at once and talk through the differences: that is delegation poker. The agreed rules go on a chart on the fridge showing who decides each thing and who must be consulted: that is the delegation matrix.

blocks.text: The vote is delegation poker; the fridge chart is the delegation matrix.

explain.body: A collaborative technique for defining decision-making within teams. Choices are typically revealed together, then differences are discussed.

test.q: Delegation poker is used to define what?
test.why: Delegation poker defines decision-making processes within teams (7.4.2).

whyNot.0: Effort is estimated with techniques such as story points.
whyNot.1: Skills are mapped in the team skill matrix.
whyNot.3: Priorities across teams are set by the CPO.

explain.body: Shows who decides and who is involved for each decision area, making authority transparent and reducing confusion and duplicated effort.

test.q: What does a delegation matrix show for each decision area?
options: Who has the skills for it
Who decides and who is involved
How long the decision will take
What it costs to make the decision
test.why: It helps teams understand who makes decisions and who is involved, according to decision area (7.4.3).

whyNot.0: Skills are shown in the skill matrix.
whyNot.2: Duration is not what the matrix records.
whyNot.3: Cost is managed through plans, not the delegation matrix.

explain.body: The team delegation matrix topic sits alongside team values and norms, the team skill matrix and team dashboards in the project kickoff workshop.

test.q: In which workshop is the team delegation matrix a topic?
test.why: The team delegation matrix is a topic of the project kickoff workshop (Table 13.8).

whyNot.0: The agile enablement workshop reviews Agilometer assessments and agile risks.
whyNot.1: The release planning workshop covers OKRs and updating the release map.
whyNot.2: The team retrospective covers the good, the bad, the learning and team building.

explain.body: Clear decision authority keeps people aligned, reduces confusion, streamlines communication and avoids duplicated effort. Clarified roles support teamwork.

test.q: Which outcome does a delegation matrix MOST directly support?
options: Higher velocity in the next stage
test.why: Making decision authority transparent ensures alignment and reduces confusion (7.4.3).

whyNot.1: Burn-down progress depends on delivered work, not on the matrix itself.
whyNot.2: Cost per iteration is a commercial and planning matter.
whyNot.3: Velocity is measured from delivered work; the matrix does not set it.
